text: {"frames":["Ferrywoman Luuk never says a word, not even when the fog rolls over the canal and her ferry bumps against the wrong dock. Her passenger, a cheese maker named Tjeerd, sets a wheel of cheese on the bench and hisses that the Tower has stolen half of it by morning. Luuk pulls a knife from her coat and cuts the wheel into twelve equal slices, then lays them in a row on the planks. From the floor above, a bell starts to ring, and Tjeerd holds out his hand for his half before it stops. How many slices make half of the wheel?","The smell of smoked cheese drifts down the Tower stairs, and Marijke's cat Pim stops on the third step to count. Pim has counted every step in Misty Ford since spring, and he always sneezes when he reaches twelve. Behind the mill wheel on the fourth floor sits a wheel of cheese that was not there yesterday, cut into twelve equal slices. A canal rat has already dragged one piece away, and Marijke needs exactly half of the slices to pay the toll at the lock. How many slices make half of the wheel?","Jorn yanks the cupboard door open, and a soft humming comes out from behind the flour sacks. It is the old song his grandmother sang over the cheese vats, and it sounds like it is coming from something small and very pleased with itself. On the shelf lies a wheel of cheese, cut into twelve equal slices that were not there last night. The humming says it will sing on until it gets exactly half, and Jorn is not sure whether to trust a voice in a cupboard. How many slices make half of the wheel?","Stop, says Alfie, and he presses his ear against the cold wall of the dyke, because the water inside the Tower is whispering. The stairs in front of them lead up to a floor that is not on any plan, and a thin voice from the top step offers them a bargain. The price is half of the wheel of cheese they carry, which has been cut into twelve equal slices by someone who would not say who. The water chuckles and says Alfie must choose the right amount before the lock gates close. How many slices make half of the wheel?","Briony wants her tulips back before the market opens, and she is already running along the dyke with a jar of fog under her arm. Overnight her neighbour Hendrik has dug up every bulb and planted them in a round bed shaped like a cheese wheel, cut into twelve equal beds. He has put a little flag in every bed and is standing at the windmill with his arms folded, waiting for her to ask. Briony has to claim half of the beds before his cart rolls onto the dyke, and the fog in her jar is already starting to leak. How many beds make half of the wheel?"]}
